meta.title: Language as Palimpsest
meta.subtitle: How empires shaped the words of Japan and Romania
meta.tagline: Language is often used as a national divider -- but it's really an international molding. Even the most isolated and nationalistic languages are composites.

examples.note: close family words remained native Japanese
close family words remained from Latin

eras.context: Both languages preserve their oldest native words for intimate, familial concepts -- the words closest to daily life resisted replacement by outside empires.

examples.note: religious and Buddhist vocabulary entered through Chinese

eras.context: Buddhism made Chinese the liturgical written language of Japan, much as South Slavonic became the liturgical written language of Romania. Sacred and scholarly words flooded in from the prestige culture.

The Ottoman Empire absorbed Romania, bringing Turkish and Arabic loanwords. Meanwhile Japan received successive waves of Chinese influence through trade and scholarship, each era's pronunciation preserved as distinct 'readings' of the same characters.

The age of exploration. European traders reached Japan, leaving words like 'pan' (bread, from Portuguese). In Romania, Austrian control of Transylvania brought Germanic influences, alongside Yiddish and Romani vocabulary.

The age of nationalism. Japan's Meiji Restoration blended English parliamentarianism and Prussian monarchy, importing words from both. Romania underwent 're-Latinization' -- purging Slavonic words and adopting French vocabulary, switching from Cyrillic to a modified Latin alphabet.

examples.note: American occupation brought a flood of English loanwords
communist ideals brought Russian political vocabulary

eras.context: After WWII, the superpowers reshaped language itself. American occupation flooded Japanese with English. Soviet domination brought Russian into Romanian -- 'tovaras' (comrade) entered everyday speech alongside communist ideology.
Both languages now absorb English at unprecedented speed. Words like 'identity' and 'democracy' arrive through screens rather than soldiers or monks -- but the pattern is ancient.

Along with the blossoming of communist ideals, words like 'comrade' enter Romanian
Culture words get imported even though Japanese words exist

kaki.note: The word 'kaki' (persimmon) traveled from Japanese to French, and then from French into Romanian -- a word that links all three languages through a single fruit.
